subject: General Knowledge
topic: Bharat Ratna & civilian awards — mixed tiers

questions.stem: On which occasion does the Government of India officially announce Padma awards each year?

options.option_text: Independence Day, the 15th of August each year
Republic Day eve, the 25th of January each year
Gandhi Jayanti, the 2nd of October each year
Constitution Day, the 26th of November each year

questions.explanation: Padma awards are announced on the eve of Republic Day (25 January) and presented by the President typically in March–April. Independence Day (15 August) is the occasion for the Prime Minister's address, not Padma announcements — a common mix-up among students.

questions.stem: The Padma awards were discontinued by the Janata Party government in 1977 and revived in which year?

options.option_text: 1975 — when Emergency was declared by Indira Gandhi
1979 — when the Janata coalition government collapsed
1980 — when Congress returned under Indira Gandhi
1983 — when the awards statute was formally re-enacted

questions.explanation: The Janata Party government suspended Padma awards in 1977 on grounds that they promoted a 'culture of sycophancy.' When the Congress returned to power under Indira Gandhi in 1980, the awards were revived. Option A (1975) is wrong — that was the Emergency; the awards were still active then.

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly matches the Bharat Ratna recipient with their primary art form?

options.option_text: Bismillah Khan — sitar maestro of the Benaras tradition
Ravi Shankar — shehnai exponent of Hindustani classical music
M.S. Subbulakshmi — Carnatic vocal music tradition
Bhimsen Joshi — tabla maestro of the Jaipur Gharana

questions.explanation: M.S. Subbulakshmi (BR 1998) is correctly identified as a Carnatic vocalist. The distractors are deliberately swapped: Bismillah Khan played the shehnai (not sitar); Ravi Shankar played the sitar (not shehnai); Bhimsen Joshi was a Hindustani vocalist of the Kirana Gharana, not a tabla player.

questions.stem: Bharat Ratna awardee Pandit Bhimsen Joshi (2009) was the foremost exponent of which Hindustani classical gharana?

options.option_text: Agra Gharana, known for dhrupad-based vocal compositions
Jaipur-Atrauli Gharana, noted for intricate melodic patterns
Kirana Gharana, renowned for sustained melodic elaboration
Patiala Gharana, celebrated for thumri and light classical styles

questions.explanation: Pandit Bhimsen Joshi was the defining voice of the Kirana Gharana, characterised by slow, deep melodic unfolding and powerful sustain (khatka-gamak). Jaipur-Atrauli is often confused with Kirana because both emphasise raag purity — but the Jaipur style is known for rhythmic complexity, not the sustained elaboration Bhimsen Joshi was celebrated for.

questions.stem: The Bharat Ratna award criteria were formally amended to include 'any field of human endeavour' in which year, paving the way for Sachin Tendulkar's recognition?

options.option_text: 2008 — during the UPA-II government's second term in office
2011 — enabling sports achievers to be recognised
2013 — the year before Tendulkar was actually conferred the award
2005 — as part of broader reforms to civilian awards criteria

questions.explanation: The original 1954 Bharat Ratna statute limited eligibility to arts, literature, science, and public service. In 2011, the UPA government amended the rules to cover 'any field of human endeavour,' which directly enabled Sachin Tendulkar's award in 2014. Option C (2013) is a trap — that was the year of announcement, not the amendment.

questions.stem: In its landmark 1996 judgment on Bharat Ratna and Padma awards, what position did the Supreme Court of India adopt?

options.option_text: These awards violate Article 18 and should be abolished by Parliament
These awards are constitutional but cannot be used as a prefix or suffix to names
These awards may be used as honorifics only by government servants in official duty
These awards are the President's prerogative and wholly outside judicial review

questions.explanation: In Balaji Raghavan vs Union of India (1996), a Constitution Bench upheld that Bharat Ratna and Padma awards do not violate Article 18 (which abolishes titles of nobility) because they are 'awards' not 'titles.' However, the Court explicitly prohibited recipients from using them as prefix or suffix to their names — a nuance that examiners frequently test. Option A is the most tempting wrong answer as Article 18 is the obvious constitutional hook.

questions.stem: Bharat Ratna awardee C. Subramaniam (conferred 1998) is historically credited with which transformative initiative as Union Agriculture Minister?

options.option_text: Launching Operation Flood to make India the world's largest milk producer
Introducing High-Yielding Variety seeds that sparked the Green Revolution
Establishing the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD)
Implementing the Integrated Rural Development Programme across backward districts

questions.explanation: Chidambaram Subramaniam, as Agriculture Minister under Indira Gandhi, championed the import and large-scale adoption of High-Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds from Mexico and Philippines in the mid-1960s, which catalysed the Green Revolution and made India self-sufficient in food grains. Option A (Operation Flood) was Verghese Kurien's work on dairy; NABARD was established in 1982 by RBI, not Subramaniam.
